blocks.title: Loan hy relative value

runs.text: The raw July equivalent is 0.294118 points higher, but ranking prices would confuse coupon, accrual and remaining cash flows with credit value. March pays 5.875% on March 1/September 1, July 5.950% on January 15/July 15. December accrual is 1.942014 versus 2.727083 per100. Both initial 2024 stubs have already occurred: March first paid September 1, 2024 after January 23 issuance; July first paid July 15, 2024 after May 13 issuance. March 2025 and January 2025 are regular scheduled coupons, not new first stubs. These calendar differences explain why price basis changes each implied yield by different amounts.

With both equivalents assumed clean (A), July adds 2.210154bp maturity yield, of which 2.049315bp is removed by the simple maturity-tenor Treasury comparison, leaving 0.160839bp. Independent ±0.5 USDm fair-value rounding yields a July-minus-March maturity gap from -0.616287 to 5.036816bp and residual gap from -2.665602 to 2.987501bp. There is no robust clean-case advantage. July's modified duration exceeds March's by 0.245358 years; a near-zero residual is not demonstrated payment for that extra risk. March is conditionally more duration-efficient if that common basis and executable levels are verified, but is not assigned Preferred.

With both equivalents assumed dirty (B), the point yield gap is 18.522010bp and residual gap 16.472695bp. Independent source rounding leaves the yield gap positive at 15.614840–21.429430bp. This signal survives rounding, but July still has 0.237119 more years of modified duration, a later maturity and different option/control mechanics; the residual is not an OAS or a quantified risk premium decomposition. No source gives the required extra compensation or executable transaction costs, so survival of rounding is necessary evidence, not sufficient proof of attractive value. Current D's basis sensitivity remains decisive, now measured on both instruments rather than just July.

Neither common basis is established. If July is clean and March dirty, July-minus-March yield is -50.936285bp; if July is dirty and March clean it is +71.668448bp. Mixed bases are possible because the disclosure does not identify either basis. These are convention scenarios, not bid/ask ranges. The price, basis, duration and call tests therefore do not jointly preserve a reliable apparent winner.

Both notes have one-month par-call windows before maturity. March's pre-window make-whole spread is Treasury+35bp; July's is +30bp. A higher discount spread reduces the remaining-payment PV and thus the premium all else equal; it is not 5bp of extra credit spread to March holders. Different schedules, remaining lives and future Treasury states preclude treating July's lower spread as a measured option-value advantage. In A each par-call leg has the lower of the two computed yields; in B maturity does for both. This two-leg minimum is not full contractual YTW. Full contingent make-whole, calendar and volatility analysis could change realized upside. July additionally expressly permits conditional redemption notice delay/rescission; no conclusion about the unreviewed March base equivalent is drawn.

The strongest contrary case to withholding preference is July B: common dirty basis, aligned executable levels preserving its net premium, no offsetting legal weakness, adequate funding certificates and an explicitly supported risk budget willing to absorb added duration would make July's additional income persuasive. The strongest March case is common clean basis, no compensating executable July residual, a lower-duration objective supported by the risk budget, and completed March legal diligence. Neither winning condition is established. Thus the choice is not a disguised forced tie: both conditional economic arguments are completed, while the missing discriminants are identified. No security is classified Secondary merely to simulate a proven Preferred peer.

blocks.note: Same-issuer bond trade-offs; loan/HY pricing inputs not supplied

runs.text: ARCC is an externally managed BDC investing mainly in middle-market debt and equity, not an industrial borrower. Annual A3 and A94 describe investment funding and swaps intended to align fixed-issued debt with a primarily floating-rate loan portfolio. Thus matched assets/liabilities, asset performance, liquidity access and valuation matter more than an invented industrial EBITDA multiple. Manager affiliation supplies operating context, not a committed support obligation. Substantially all investments lack readily available quotations; A96/A99 explicitly warn that forced realizations can be materially below reported values. That uncertainty affects the assets supporting these unsecured claims, not merely accounting volatility.

The source-backed upstream fundamental view is mixed, not blanket deterioration. A116 shows investment income 2990 versus 2614 USDm and NII 1403 versus 1266; net operations are 1522 in both years, while diluted EPS is 2.44 versus 2.68. Higher NII is a substantive debt-service countercase, but aggregate growth does not establish recurring cash realization or per-share growth. A73 nonaccruals rose from 1.3% to 1.7% at amortized cost and 0.6% to 1.0% at fair value; average internal grade remained 3.1. Grade 4 is the issuer's best grade, opposite the CP-3 risk-score direction; 3.1 is not imported as a CP-3 score. The two quality signals must coexist.

A255 CFO of -2128 versus +511 USDm includes purchases -12622 and sales/repayments 9212, plus PIK interest/dividend adjustments -206/-257 and collections +109/+33 in 2024. These are portfolio deployment and realization flows, not industrial cash burn or a CFO-minus-capex FCF measure. A115 ordinary cash 635 is distinct from restricted cash 225 and cash-flow ending combined cash 860. Debt caption 13727 and separate Secured borrowings 32 remain separate; neither is silently redefined. A255 distributions paid 1139 and common issuance proceeds 1364 show cash outflows and new capital together, not a debt-funded recap or assured equity backstop. A89 reports no open-market program repurchases in 2024/2023. Governance concerns here are valuation incentives and cash-retention trade-offs; neither managerial support nor adverse conduct is presumed.

C's current July finding of published 196.2% coverage versus 150% supports a historical financing-flexibility countercase; it is not freely drawable cash or dollar capacity. The facility's separate maintenance, equity and borrowing-base requirements can constrain access before payment default, and C does not supply its actual tested ratio. A88's approximately 5.1bn conditional facility availability cannot simply be added to cash without testing restrictions and uses. The nearest supported pressure point is weaker borrower performance/marks reducing coverage and collateral eligibility; funding access could then tighten, forcing more reliance on collections, asset sales or equity before refinancing dated parent maturities. This is a conditional causal pathway, not a forecast of default. The initiating observables are nonaccruals, realization versus marks, borrowing-base reports, certificates, actual draws and executed returns.

The strongest issuer-level contrary case is higher NII, unchanged average grade, positive published coverage, dated issuer compliance assertions and subsequent January 2025 market issuance. It wins against immediate funding-closure claims if transaction-date certificates demonstrate surviving pro forma Act coverage, facility maintenance/equity/base tests, lender commitments and accessible cash after uses. Those inputs are not supplied. Therefore conviction is higher in the historical facts than in future liquidity sufficiency. No borrower-level valuation, complete funding forecast, ratings/trigger review or governing factor weights supports a composite or rating tier.

blocks.title: What changed since the last Report

runs.text: The strongest supported market signal is a positive but convention-sensitive July 2029 yield premium to Treasury, not a distress verdict or a security preference. A291's 861 USDm Level 2 fair value divided by 850 USDm principal produces an evaluated equivalent, not an observed executable clean price. Unknown basis alone moves the maturity yield by about 69.458294bp between A and B—far more than the roughly 1.5bp rounding sensitivity within each case. Under A the June 15, 2029 par-call leg has the lower yield; under B maturity does. That reversal makes it especially important not to silently declare a unique contractual yield-to-worst. Source fair values improved versus 2023 for the eight continuing series, but those point changes exclude coupons, reinvestment and trading costs and are not total returns. The low 86 equivalent for the 3.200% November 2031 series cannot establish relative credit weakness versus a 7.000% January 2027 series above par.

Evidence → mechanism → creditor consequence: A94's swaps align issuer funding with a primarily floating-rate loan portfolio; this is BDC matched funding, not industrial EBITDA leverage. A95's unsecured payment ranking gives equal payment status against non-subordinated unsecured debt, but collateral priority and subsidiary claims reduce direct asset access separately. C4's published 196.2% statutory coverage against 150% supports historical financing flexibility; a fall in portfolio values would reduce the coverage numerator, potentially tighten borrowing-base eligibility and funding access, and make refinancing maturing parent debt more dependent on asset repayments/sales or equity. Added secured borrowing could preserve cash while reducing unsecured access to pledged value. No numerical recovery or probability follows from those mechanisms.

The strongest supported countercase is the positive historical 46.2 percentage-point published coverage margin, the issuer's dated material-compliance assertions, conditional funding access, and subsequent January 2025 capital-market issuance (A95; C4 T4C.4, T4C.5). It would win against an immediate funding-closure thesis if dated certificates demonstrated adequate pro forma coverage, borrowing-base eligibility, equity tests, lender commitments and accessible cash after intended uses. Those conditions are not supplied, so this countercase reduces conviction in distress inference without proving value or implementation readiness. The initiating deterioration to monitor is weaker loan performance/marks; the first financial break would be lost asset backing or funding eligibility, followed by restricted liquidity and more expensive or constrained refinancing. Observable tests are coverage disclosures, facility certificates, portfolio marks, actual draws and shareholder-return execution—not an unsupported generic recession shock.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: **Legal formula versus interpretation.** Base §10.07 undertakes not to violate the specified Act provisions, modified by §61(a), successors and Commission relief, whether or not the issuer is otherwise subject to them. The annual reports the applicable minimum reduced to 150% effective June 21, 2019 and measured after borrowing (A274). The first supplement controls conflicts for this series only (§§7.04,7.06). It does not replace §10.07 with an EBITDA test. Specified SBA debenture relief in A65 must remain specific; it is not permission to exclude all subsidiary debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: This is an **incurrence/issuance comparison**, not an independently continuously tested 150% note-maintenance assertion. A276 adds a materially different fact: the issuer describes a facility obligation to maintain a 1.5 ratio, stockholders' equity, borrowing-base and other restrictions. It also states compliance in all material respects with that facility at December 31, 2024. That is the issuer's dated assertion, not an independently certified test or present-day all-contract compliance conclusion. The published Act ratio cannot silently serve as the facility's actual tested ratio merely because both minima are numerically 1.5.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: These thirteen routes distinguish demonstrated note permissions, issuer summaries, and evidence gaps. Ratio/acquisition/refinancing debt, incremental equivalent debt, free-and-clear amounts, fixed/grower/general baskets and junior debt payments are not silently zero or absent: their independent legal availability and utilization remain unresolved in G2/G5/G6. There is no support for aggregating them. The 5.1bn conditional aggregate facility availability, 3,348 USDm revolver availability and 2,219 USDm ceiling difference are different quantities; the first includes the second, and the third is not a further liquidity source.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: **Separate remedies and lender control.** Base §5.01(vii), p12/L917, requires coverage **below 100% on the last business day of each of 24 consecutive calendar months**. This is neither the 150% after-borrowing test nor a general two-year cure period. Supplement §4.03, pp2–3/L216–217, separately requires failure to comply with other agreements in the notes/indenture for **60 consecutive calendar days after written notice** from the Trustee or holders of at least **25%** principal. It does not make every external agreement breach subject to that same limb; the distinct borrowed-debt cross-default provision is S §4.04. Under S §4.06, a continuing non-bankruptcy Event of Default permits declaration by Trustee or 25% holders; the specified bankruptcy limbs have automatic consequences. No actual breach, notice, monthly history or acceleration is inferred here.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: General amendment authority in B §9.02 is majority-based, with affected-holder exceptions including specified §10.07 changes and payment rights. Past-default waiver exceptions in B §5.13 also matter. Covenant defeasance is permitted for §§10.07–10.08 by S §1.01(g), but requires B §§14.03–14.04 conditions, including sufficient irrevocable trust funding, non-conflict/no-default conditions, tax opinion and certificates. No actual election or satisfaction is supplied. These conditions prevent both extremes: protection cannot be assumed permanent, and a majority cannot simply be assumed able to erase all relevant rights.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The series' change-of-control offer is **100% of principal plus accrued unpaid interest**, not TDG's 101% and not a market price or recovery floor (S pp2–3, §2.01 and Art Six). It requires both defined Change of Control and Below Investment Grade Rating Event: all three agencies below investment grade within the defined window, with attribution requirements. Permitted-holder exclusions matter. Full redemption and a qualifying third-party offer can remove the issuer-offer requirement; timing, lawful-payment, securities-law and Act-related extension conditions apply. This is contingent liquidity protection, not unconditional put capacity today.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: **Pressure Point:** erosion of the selected notes' asset-coverage-based debt-incurrence cushion. **Evidence:** B §10.07 and A65/A274 support published 1.962x against a reported 1.5x after-borrowing minimum. **Risk Mechanic:** portfolio valuation declines reduce the adjusted asset numerator; borrowing adds senior debt and its proceeds/use changes assets; cash-funded distributions reduce assets, while debt-funded distributions can both add debt and remove proceeds. The resulting financing restriction can arrive before a payment default. **Credit Implication:** less room to finance commitments or refinance debt can force asset sales, repayment or equity funding; reduced asset backing also matters to unsecured creditors, without an asserted recovery value. **Monitoring Signal:** next coverage disclosure, pro forma borrowing certificate, portfolio marks, actual draws and executed shareholder returns. **Evidence Needed to Tighten View:** unrounded numerator/denominator, relief bridge, funding uses, facility certificate and accessible-asset schedule. The facility maintenance test receives preference only when near-term breach relevance is evidenced; here its actual headroom is missing, so it cannot displace this quantified incurrence pressure point. No claim is made that this is the group's mathematically tightest covenant.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Ares Capital Corporation has **limited covenant-capacity visibility**. The main capacity concern is erosion of asset-coverage-based incurrence room, because falling investment values or funded shareholder returns can reduce the ability to raise debt precisely when liquidity is needed. Exact headroom is supported **only at published precision**, not as unrounded certified headroom or actual usable dollars. Further analysis requires the G1–G6 inputs below. The principal documented points are the positive historical cushion; conditional rather than freely available secured financing; unquantified RP/leakage permissions and utilization; and an asset-value definition rather than an EBITDA add-back engine. The single nearest pressure point above governs the capacity challenge, not an unsupported distress narrative.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest contrary case is substantive: reported coverage exceeds the applicable minimum, cash is reported, substantial conditional facility availability is disclosed, and the issuer asserts facility compliance in all material respects at the balance-sheet date. The January 2025 issuance also evidences subsequent capital-market access. That countercase would win against a claim of immediate funding closure if transaction-date certificates show that adequate coverage, borrowing-base eligibility, equity requirements, lender commitments and accessible cash survive the intended uses. The source pack does not establish all those conditions. Accordingly, conviction is higher in the historical ratio comparison than in an available-cash inference. This narrows implementation to documentary follow-up and monitoring; absent price, portfolio mandate and current evidence, it does not support action or sizing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: **Subsequent events, not December adjustments.** A300 reports January 2025 issuance of **1,000 USDm**, **5.800%** notes due March 8, 2032. Related forward-starting swap notional is 1,000 USDm, effective **January 8, 2026**, receiving 5.800% and paying one-month SOFR plus 1.6995%. This is distinct from the July 2029 coupon of 5.950% and its 6.040% effective stated rate including swap (A282); none is an asset-coverage input. A300–301 reports February 2025 extension of the existing up-to-1,000 USDm common-stock repurchase program from February 15, 2025 to February 15, 2026, under stated price/legal conditions and issuer discretion. It is authority, not an executed 1,000 USDm outflow or known unused balance. No unsupported post-event coverage is calculated: net new-debt uses, actual repurchases and intervening asset/liability changes are missing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No full current compliance assertion, automatic default, industrial shock, PD estimate or recovery percentage is supported. Unknown routes stay unknown rather than disappearing from the analysis. These gaps restrict the relevant outputs, not the supported published subtraction. They should be resolved with bounded document requests, preserving the December 2024 anchor rather than quietly replacing it with a later balance sheet.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: **CP-6 should actively test, not inherit, the strongest favorable inference:** does 1.962x coverage plus reported conditional funding access actually permit the proposed borrowing and preserve a usable liquidity buffer after intended uses? Require G1/G2 transaction and facility certificates, reconcile proceeds retained/invested/distributed, locate accessible cash and collateral, and prevent addition of the revolver subamount or ceiling difference to aggregate availability. The bear challenge should trace observable portfolio marks or executed returns through adjusted assets and funding constraints before discussing default. The favorable case must show conditions surviving, not merely repeat the headline 5.1bn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Monitoring should pair each coverage disclosure with borrowing-base availability, maintenance certificates, encumbrance changes, actual shareholder-return execution, new debt uses and notices/consents. Re-test on new draws, asset-value changes, repurchases or amendments. CP-3C/CP-2D can then assess refinancing and liquidity; CP-3 and CP-6A need price and portfolio context before security selection or sizing. CP-5 should audit the legal/financial traces and historical lineage. **None of these downstream challenges or modules is claimed to have run.**
